rebuilds.why: Option B "£4.3" equals the key £4.30 in value (maths-31 put the slip in the answer, not the working), so it was a second correct answer. Replaced by £5.30, the carried pound added twice (maths-13, as on MC03-MEAS-06 and MC05-GEOM-01). Walk script trap line rewritten to name the two remaining carry mistakes; executions written for C and D, which had none.

stem.text: Anya buys a ruler for £1.70 and a pen for £2.60. What is the total cost?

options.execution: The child adds 70p and 60p to make 130p, writes 30p and carries £1, but adds the £1 twice into the pounds: 1 + 2 + 1 + 1 = 5. That gives £5.30 instead of £4.30.
The child adds 70p and 60p to make 130p but keeps only the 30p and drops the carried £1, adding whole pounds 1 + 2 = 3. That gives £3.30 instead of £4.30.
The child rounds £1.70 up to £2 and £2.60 up to £3 and gives the rounded total, £5.00. The real prices are 30p and 40p less, so the total is £4.30.

explanationPatch.walkScript: Add the two prices, pounds and pence together. Seventy pence plus sixty pence makes £1.30. That carries to give £4.30 in total. A trap loses the carried pound, or adds it twice.
explanationPatch._previousWalkScript: Add the two prices, pounds and pence together. Seventy pence plus sixty pence makes £1.30. That carries to give £4.30 in total. A trap drops the pence zero, or the carried pound.

notes.MC05-MEAS-03: £4.3 (same value as the key) → £5.30 (maths-13). Options £4.30*, £5.30, £3.30, £5.00. Arithmetic: 1.70 + 2.60 = 4.30; carry added twice 1+2+1+1 = 5 → £5.30; carry dropped → £3.30; both rounded up 2 + 3 = £5.00.
